clues: This city lies north of Mexico City, in a wide valley region. It sits a short trip from the capital of its own state.
Rain peaks here twice a year, around June and again in September. By contrast, February and December are the driest months of the year.
The city was founded on a July day in fifteen forty six. People still mark that founding day with a party each July.
This town is widely known for its food, above all for ximbo and barbacoa. Those two dishes sit at the heart of its fame.
Its best known landmark is the Church and ex-convent of San Nicolás de Tolentino. No other sight in town points to the answer as clearly as it does.
